rationale: Complete PMC HTML body for the AOPMC Abstracts 2025 supplement (Mov Disord Clin Pract. 2025;12 Suppl 1:S18–S300; DOI 10.1002/mdc3.14359) reviewed. Abstract 114, “Aromatic Plants and Parkinson’s Disease: The Science and Secrets,” reviews essential oils and cites the 2021 Origanum majorana tea pilot, but does not test odor identification or olfactory impairment; its only human outcome detail is NMSS and Beck Depression Inventory. In that abstract Origanum majorana occurs only in a reference, not intervention. This is indirect review context, not a food-specific smell result.

Official OUP issue record confirms this is the Abstracts of the 11th International Congress on Schizophrenia Research, volume 33 issue 2 (March 2007), pp.203–631, DOI 10.1093/schbul/sbm004. Public issue record is metadata/abstract listing; full publisher PDF is subscriber-only. An HKU repository page exposes one individual p.214 abstract, “Cognitive correlates of semantic language disorder in first-episode schizophrenia,” unrelated to marjoram/smell, but that member does not cover the full issue. Keep pending pending full collection access.

Complete poster supplement PDF (FEBS Open Bio 2022;12 Suppl 1:67–336; DOI 10.1002/2211-5463.13440) reviewed from University of Nova de Lisboa repository copy; source identity/header and pagination match publisher citation. P-01.4-012 (printed p.149) tests Greek dittany, thyme and sage extracts in RAW264.7 macrophages for cytotoxicity/anti-inflammatory/antioxidant measures. A separate P-01.2-001 AD rat poster mentions apathy for cotinine/6-hydroxynicotine. No same-report thyme/apathy intervention or human Parkinson endpoint.

Complete 306-page original congress abstract scan reviewed (Journal of Neurology. 1985;232 Suppl 1:1–306; DOI 10.1007/BF02428072). PMC article/publisher title is XIIth World Congress of Neurology; PubMed PMID 4067611 incorrectly labels it XIIIth, although date/place/volume/DOI/PMCID identify the same source. OCR thyme hits are scan errors for thymic/thymus (e.g., printed p.38 myasthenia/thymic pathology; page image confirms). Apathy occurs separately in the printed p.181 pellagra/nutritional-deficiency report. No culinary thyme or same-report apathy.

Complete PMC HTML body reviewed. The only Origanum majorana reference is in abstract 114’s review of aromatic plants and Parkinson’s disease; that review reports NMSS and Beck Depression Inventory for its human evidence and no dystonia endpoint. The supplement’s other dystonia abstracts are different reports/interventions. This is indirect reference context only, not marjoram treatment of dystonia.

Official PMC landing page identifies “Administrative content — journal masthead, notices, indexes, etc.” in Am J Hum Genet. 1996 Oct;59(Suppl):i2. It provides a scanned 43.8-MB PDF link but no body text in its HTML. Direct PDF route returned a PMC download-preparation interstitial, and OA package route is unavailable. Original scan body not examined; retain pending without inferring no dystonia content.

Official OUP records pp.203–631 for the full 2007 congress abstract collection but marks its PDF subscriber-only. HKU repository p.214 abstract is cognitive-language disorder in first-episode schizophrenia and contains no food/dystonia; it is one member only. Full collection/member matching marjoram–dystonia remains unresolved and pending.

Complete official PMC text searched. Abstract 114 (Aromatic Plants and Parkinson’s Disease) cites a 2021 Origanum majorana tea pilot but describes no facial-expression or hypomimia outcome; it gives only NMSS and Beck Depression Inventory for the one human trial. Facial/hypomimia references elsewhere belong to separate abstracts/interventions. The citation is indirect marjoram/PD context, not fresh marjoram changing facial expression.

Complete 270-page FEBS Open Bio posters supplement (same DOI 10.1002/2211-5463.13440) searched. Culinary basil is explicitly identified as Ocimum basilicum L. in poster P-05.1-021, “Antioxidant content of basil leaves … different colors” (printed p.308); it compares antioxidant constituents in green/purple leaf samples. Apathy occurs only in separate poster P-01.2-001 on cotinine/6-hydroxynicotine in an Alzheimer rat model. No basil/apathy report-level match or human Parkinson outcome.
